Human-in-the-Loop

Configure human approval for sensitive tool operations.

graph LR %% Main Entry Agent[Agent] --> Interrupt{Interrupt?} %% Decision Logic Interrupt -->|no| Execute[Execute] Interrupt -->|yes| Human{Human} %% Human Interaction Paths Human -->|approve| Execute Human -->|edit| Execute Human -->|reject| Cancel[Cancel] %% Feedback Loops Execute --> Agent Cancel --> Agent

Basic Configuration

Use the interrupt_on parameter to specify which tools require approval. You must also provide a checkpointer.

from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

checkpointer = MemorySaver()

agent = create_deep_agent(
    tools=[delete_file, read_file],
    interrupt_on={
        "delete_file": True,  # Default: approve, edit, reject
        "read_file": False,   # No interrupts
    },
    checkpointer=checkpointer # Required!
)

Decision Types

When an interrupt occurs, the user can provide one of the following decisions:

  • "approve": Execute with original arguments.
  • "edit": Modify arguments before execution.
  • "reject": Skip execution entirely.

Handling Interrupts

When the agent pauses, you can inspect the __interrupt__ key in the result and provide a decision.

# Check for interrupt
if result.get("__interrupt__"):
    interrupts = result["__interrupt__"][0].value
    action_requests = interrupts["action_requests"]
    
    # Decisions match action_requests order
    decisions = [{"type": "approve"}] 

    # Resume execution with the command
    result = agent.invoke(
        Command(resume={"decisions": decisions}),
        config=config
    )

Multiple Tool Calls

If multiple tools are called in parallel, you must provide a decision for each one, in the same order as they appear in action_requests.

decisions = [
    {"type": "approve"}, # For tool call 1
    {"type": "reject"}   # For tool call 2
]

Editing Tool Arguments

You can modify the tool arguments on the fly by using the "edit" decision type.

decisions = [{
    "type": "edit",
    "edited_action": {
        "name": "send_email",
        "args": {"to": "[email protected]", "subject": "Fixed subject"}
    }
}]

Subagent Interrupts

Subagents can have their own interrupt configurations. These override or extend the main agent's settings.

Best Practices

Always use a checkpointer

Human-in-the-loop requires state persistence to pause and resume execution. Always pass a checkpointer to create_deep_agent.

Use the same thread ID

To resume a conversation, you must use the same thread_id in the config for both the initial call and the resume call.

config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "my-thread"}}
# Initial call
agent.invoke(input, config=config)
# Resume call
agent.invoke(Command(resume={...}), config=config)

Match decision order to actions

Ensure your list of decisions matches the length and order of action_requests.

decisions = []
for action in action_requests:
    # Logic to get user decision
    decision = get_user_decision(action) 
    decisions.append(decision)

Tailor configurations by risk

You can customize allowed decisions based on the risk level of the tool.

interrupt_on = {
    # High risk: full control
    "delete_file": {"allowed_decisions": ["approve", "edit", "reject"]},
    
    # Medium risk: no editing allowed
    "write_file": {"allowed_decisions": ["approve", "reject"]},
    
    # Low risk: no interrupts
    "read_file": False, 
}
